description: Real-card synthetic binder regression corpus built from actual Pokémon card metadata and locally cached real card images, with page-level layout, pricing rollups, and scanner-evaluation demos.

pricing_reference.notes: Prices are intentionally synthetic-but-plausible so regression tests stay stable even when live market prices move.

pages.label: Page 1 · starter hits
notes: all cards are front-facing
clean sleeves
dense but readable 3x3 binder layout

pages.label: Page 2 · glare, duplicates, and an empty pocket
notes: includes sleeve glare on two hits
fully populated with real-card references
duplicate pricing should still roll up correctly

pages.label: Page 3 · lower-value depth and repeated commons
notes: mixes lower-value cards with one strong mid-tier hit
repeats commons to test duplicate grouping
all slots are populated to exercise full-page pricing

pages.label: Page 4 · illustration rare showcase
notes: designed to stress high-cardinality identification
mostly illustration rares with similar layouts
no empty pockets on this page

pages.label: Page 5 · mixed conditions and older pulls
notes: conditions vary from near mint to damaged
fully populated with older real-card references
includes promos and several played holos

pages.label: Page 6 · modern chase cards
notes: high-end modern cards concentrate binder value
mixes SIRs, gold cards, and meta staples
helpful for testing price concentration summaries

pages.label: Page 7 · gallery page with duplicates and budget hits
notes: contains multiple mid-tier gallery cards
repeats a few cards from earlier pages
now fully populated for dense binder evaluation

pages.label: Page 8 · premium finishers and recognizable benchmarks
notes: contains several cards collectors instantly recognize
intended for top-end binder total regression
includes strong page-level price concentration

pages.label: Page 9 · binder closer with trainers and fan favorites
notes: balances trainers, cute illustration rares, and playable cards
keeps the dataset from being all high-dollar chases
fully populated final page

pages.label: Page 10 · premium alternate-art showcase
notes: stresses top-end valuation and recognizable grails
contains multiple benchmark chase cards for sanity checks
no empty pockets on this page

pages.label: Page 11 · supporter and trainer value page
notes: trainer page helps test non-Pokémon title matching
mixes modern SIRs with lower-value full-art supporters
still fully populated for dense page scoring

pages.label: Page 12 · eeveelution favorites and fan-service hits
notes: combines promos, alt arts, and gallery cards
all nine slots now use real card references
useful for duplicate and near-duplicate naming tests

pages.label: Page 13 · premium gallery legends
notes: gallery cards share similar framing and can confuse coarse classifiers
intended to stress duplicate groups and mid/high-tier totals
fully populated comparison page

pages.label: Page 14 · edition and budget edge cases
notes: contains side-by-side unlimited and 1st-edition Jungle Pikachu scans
used to verify picture-only edition-sensitive identification
keeps mild long-tail pricing behavior on the back page

pages.label: Page 15 · adversarial scanner breakage cases
notes: extreme skew, motion blur, occlusion bands, and heavy sleeve glare
includes near-duplicate Pikachu and eeveelution cases meant to fool image matching
intentionally hard enough that the current scanner should miss some cards

pages.label: Page 16 · eeveelution adversarial confusion
notes: multiple visually similar eeveelution V and VMAX cards under heavy corruption
mixes blur, glare, occlusion, and zoom crop to trigger cross-matching errors
intended to break naive template matching on similar artwork families

pages.label: Page 17 · modern ex glare and crop traps
notes: modern ex cards with bright foil-like art are combined with hard glare and cropping
similar yellow and purple palettes are meant to trigger false nearest-neighbor matches
tests how badly the baseline scanner degrades on strong specular highlights

pages.label: Page 18 · vintage edition and promo degradation
notes: vintage and promo cards are intentionally washed out, blurred, and partly covered
includes both edition-sensitive and low-detail older layouts that are hard to separate
meant to stress failures on older scans with weaker local features

pages.label: Page 19 · trainer and support card hard mode
notes: text-heavy trainers and supporters are degraded with blur and color shifts
designed to break matching where artwork is less dominant and typography matters more
keeps the corpus from only failing on flashy Pokémon cards

pages.label: Page 20 · mixed adversarial benchmark
notes: combines modern, vintage, promo, and gallery cards under the harshest synthetic conditions so far
acts as a broad stress benchmark rather than a narrow one-family confusion page
expected to keep the baseline scanner failing until a stronger recognition approach is added

pages.label: Page 21 · vintage ex destruction set
notes: high-value vintage ex cards rendered with severe blur, glare, and occlusion
aims to create expensive mispricing, not just harmless misclassifications
keeps pressure on both identification and binder-total estimation

pages.label: Page 22 · supporter OCR nightmare
notes: supporter-heavy page where text boxes are washed out or smeared
intended to expose how brittle the scanner is when artwork alone is not enough
useful for future work on text-aware or layout-aware recognition

pages.label: Page 23 · starter-line similarity traps
notes: evolution lines and closely related starters are mixed together under hard distortions
focuses on cards that can share colors or silhouettes after blur and cropping
acts as a low-level recognition stress page rather than a rarity-driven page

pages.label: Page 24 · dragon and vstar collapse cases
notes: dragon, dark, and cosmic vstar cards are pushed into severe blur and skew
targets dramatic artwork families that still confuse under image corruption
useful for measuring whether the scanner latches onto color clouds instead of structure

pages.label: Page 25 · water-electric adversarial mix
notes: blue and yellow-heavy cards are combined to provoke palette-based false matches
includes both old and new printing styles on the same page
especially useful for checking confusion between Pikachu, Raichu, Jolteon, and water cards

pages.label: Page 26 · promo chaos page
notes: promos from multiple eras with inconsistent framing and art styles
intentionally mixes low-detail and high-detail promo cards under ugly imaging conditions
helps ensure the hard set is not dominated by a single release family

pages.label: Page 27 · kanto nostalgia grind
notes: older-style Kanto cards, fossils, and starter-era nostalgia cards under harsh image degradation
built to stress the scanner on flatter art and simpler layouts
adds diversity beyond full-art modern cards and ex cards

pages.label: Page 28 · modern full-art collapse
notes: full-art modern hits with similar saturated gradients are intentionally mauled
designed to produce plausible but wrong matches among expensive flashy cards
useful for measuring whether expensive pages create catastrophic total errors

pages.label: Page 29 · eeveelution sequel hard mode
notes: another eeveelution-heavy page, but with different card mix and more promo/vstar variants
extends the original page-16 idea so the failure bank is not a single page
good future target for model improvements that should generalize across similar families

pages.label: Page 30 · maximum degradation benchmark
notes: the harshest blended benchmark page in the corpus so far
mixes valuable vintage cards, edition-sensitive cards, and modern full-art cards under extreme corruption
intended to remain a durable failing benchmark even after modest scanner improvements

pages.label: Page 31 · single card layout probe
notes: single large pocket layout to verify the scanner can detect a lone card from image pixels alone
intended as a smoke test for non-grid-9 counting before harder layout cases

pages.label: Page 32 · two-up layout probe
notes: two-card spread layout to verify the scanner does not assume three columns
kept relatively easy so layout detection is what is being exercised, not adversarial corruption

pages.label: Page 33 · six-up layout probe
notes: six-card 3x2 page to verify automatic card counting beyond a square 3x3 assumption
uses moderate glare and tilt but is primarily a layout-regression page

pages.label: Page 34 · twelve-up layout probe
notes: twelve-card 4x3 page to verify denser layouts remain scannable from image pixels alone
acts as a layout-coverage page rather than an adversarial breakage page

pages.label: Page 35 · random scattered layout A
notes: five cards scattered irregularly across the page instead of following a clean grid
intended to expose how much the current layout-template scanner depends on regular structure

pages.label: Page 36 · random scattered layout B
notes: seven cards scattered with uneven spacing and row breaks
a denser irregular page for counting and ordering stress

pages.label: Page 37 · random scattered layout C
notes: four larger cards placed in asymmetric corners and center areas
acts as a sparse irregular-layout stress page

pages.label: Page 38 · random scattered layout D
notes: eight-card irregular scatter page mixing vintage, promo, and trainer cards
useful for seeing how badly the current scanner degrades once no supported layout template really fits
